items.e: 5/8 = 0.625 and 2/3 is about 0.667, so the correct order is 0.6, then 5/8, then 2/3, then 0.7.
items.q: Which list is in order from least to greatest?

items.e: 350 divided by 25 is 14 bottles per minute, and 1 hour 20 minutes is 80 minutes, so 80 x 14 = 1,120 bottles.
items.q: A machine fills 350 bottles in 25 minutes at a steady rate. At that rate, how many bottles does it fill in 1 hour and 20 minutes?

items.e: A 25% increase makes the price $75, and 20% of $75 is $15, so the final price is $75 - $15 = $60.
items.q: A jacket costs $60. The store raises the price by 25%, then later takes 20% off the new price. What is the final price?

items.e: The two sides must add to 18, half of the perimeter, and multiply to 72; 6 + 12 = 18 and 6 x 12 = 72.
items.q: A rectangle has an area of 72 square centimeters and a perimeter of 36 centimeters. What are its side lengths?

items.e: Doubling adds the remainder to itself: 4 + 4 = 8, and 8 is one more than 7, so the new remainder is 1 (for example, 11 leaves 4 and 22 leaves 1).
items.q: When a whole number is divided by 7, the remainder is 4. What is the remainder when twice that number is divided by 7?

c: The product of two even numbers is always divisible by 8.
The sum of an even number and an odd number is always odd.
The sum of two odd numbers is always even.
The product of two odd numbers is always odd.
items.e: 2 x 2 = 4, which is not divisible by 8, so the last statement is false; the other three are always true.
items.q: Which of these statements is FALSE?

items.e: A square has 4 equal sides, so the perimeter is 4 × 7 = 28 inches.
items.q: A square photo frame has sides that are 7 inches long. What is the perimeter of the frame?

items.e: Three layers of 8 cubes each is 3 × 8 = 24 cubes.
items.q: A box is filled with unit cubes. Each layer holds 8 cubes, and the box is 3 layers tall. How many unit cubes does the box hold in all?

items.e: The tank holds 8×5×6=240 cubic inches and already has 8×5×3=120, so 240−120=120 more are needed.
items.q: A rectangular tank is 8 inches long, 5 inches wide, and 6 inches deep. Water in it is 3 inches deep. How many more cubic inches of water are needed to fill the tank?

items.e: With nine values listed in order, the median is the 5th one, and the 5th age in the list is 10.
items.q: The ages of nine students are listed in order: 8, 9, 9, 10, 10, 11, 11, 12, 13. What is the median age?

items.e: The shop sold 12+18+9+15+21=75 books, but the goal needed 5×16=80, so it fell 5 books short.
items.q: A shop records books sold: Monday 12, Tuesday 18, Wednesday 9, Thursday 15, Friday 21. The goal was to average 16 books per day over the five days. How many more books would the shop have had to sell that week to meet the goal?

items.e: Adding 5° to every value raises the highest and the lowest by the same amount, so the range stays 14°.
items.q: One week of daily high temperatures has a range of 14°. The next week, every daily high is exactly 5° warmer than the matching day of the first week. What is the range of the second week's highs?

items.e: Grade 5 read 7×8=56 books and Grade 4 read 5 1/2×8=44, so the difference is 56−44=12.
items.q: In a pictograph, one book symbol stands for 8 books read. Grade 4 shows 5 1/2 symbols and Grade 5 shows 7 symbols. How many more books did Grade 5 read than Grade 4?

items.e: Both perimeters are 24 m, but the areas are 4×8=32 and 6×6=36, so Pen 2 is 36−32=4 square meters larger.
items.q: Two rectangular pens each use exactly 24 meters of fencing. Pen 1 measures 4 m by 8 m and Pen 2 measures 6 m by 6 m. How much greater is the area of Pen 2?

c: Bag X, because it has more red marbles
Bag X, because it holds more marbles in all
Bag Y, because 3/8 is greater than 1/3
items.e: Bag X gives 4/12=1/3 and Bag Y gives 3/8; since 1/3=8/24 and 3/8=9/24, Bag Y is more likely.
items.q: Bag X holds 4 red and 8 blue marbles. Bag Y holds 3 red and 5 blue marbles. From which bag is drawing a red marble more likely?

items.e: The first rug covers 6×4=24 sq ft; the second is 18 by 2, or 36 sq ft, and 36÷24=1 1/2. Tripling one side and halving the other multiplies the area by 3×1/2.
items.q: A rug is 6 feet long and 4 feet wide. A second rug is 3 times as long and half as wide as the first. How does the area of the second rug compare with the area of the first?

items.e: The five numbers total 5×14=70 and all six total 6×15=90, so the added number is 90−70=20.
items.q: The mean of five numbers is 14. A sixth number is added, and the mean of all six numbers is 15. What is the sixth number?

items.e: If each equal angle is x, then x+x+(x+30)=180, so 3x=150 and x=50; the largest angle is 50+30=80°.
items.q: In a triangle, two of the angles are equal and the third angle is 30° larger than each of them. What is the measure of the largest angle?

items.e: A whole number is divisible by 5 when its last digit is 0 or 5, and 75 ends in 5 while the others end in 2, 8, and 4.
items.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 5?

items.e: Each foot is 12 inches, so 4 feet is 4 × 12 = 48 inches.
items.q: A rope is 4 feet long. How many inches long is the rope? (1 foot = 12 inches)

items.e: The rate is 42÷6=7 pages per minute, so in 15 minutes it prints 7×15=105 pages.
items.q: A printer prints 42 pages in 6 minutes at a steady rate. How many pages does it print in 15 minutes?

items.e: Each number is 5 less than the one before it, so the next number is 30 − 5 = 25.
items.q: The numbers in a pattern are 45, 40, 35, 30, ... . What is the next number in the pattern?

items.e: 25% of $80 is $20, so the marked-down price is $60, and $60−$5=$55.
items.q: A jacket priced at $80 is marked down 25%. At the register, another $5 is taken off. What is the final price?

items.e: Adding the four weeks gives 4 + 7 + 5 + 6 = 22 goals.
items.q: A team records its goals each week: Week 1 has 4 goals, Week 2 has 7 goals, Week 3 has 5 goals, and Week 4 has 6 goals. How many goals did the team score in the four weeks altogether?

items.e: The primes from 1 to 10 are 2, 3, 5, and 7 — four of the ten cards — so the probability is 4/10=2/5.
items.q: Ten cards numbered 1 through 10 are placed face down and one is drawn at random. What is the probability that the card drawn shows a prime number?

items.e: In twelfths, 1/3=4/12 and 1/2=6/12, and 5/12 falls between them; 1/4 is smaller and 3/5 and 2/3 are larger than 1/2.
items.q: Which fraction is between 1/3 and 1/2?

items.e: Using 24ths, 2/3=16/24 and 5/8=15/24, so she needs 16/24−15/24=1/24 of a yard.
items.q: Priya has 5/8 of a yard of ribbon but needs 2/3 of a yard. How much more ribbon does she need?

items.e: The whole sheet is 10×6=60 square cm and the piece removed is 3×4=12, so 60−12=48 square cm remain.
items.q: A rectangular sheet of paper is 10 cm by 6 cm. A 3 cm by 4 cm rectangle is cut away from one corner. What is the area of the piece that is left?

items.e: The fourth vertex shares the x-value 1 with (1, 5) and the y-value 2 with (9, 2), giving (1, 2).
items.q: Three vertices of a rectangle are (1, 5), (9, 5), and (9, 2). What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex?

items.e: Rounding gives 4,200+3,900+2,900=11,000, and the exact total, 10,955, is much closer to 11,000 than to 10,000.
items.q: A stadium sold 4,180 tickets on Friday, 3,905 on Saturday, and 2,870 on Sunday. Which is the best estimate of the total number of tickets sold?

items.e: The pencils cost 3×$0.30=$0.90, leaving $1.30−$0.90=$0.40 for two erasers, so one eraser is $0.20.
items.q: Three pencils and two erasers cost $1.30 in all. One pencil costs $0.30. What does one eraser cost?

items.e: The five scores total 5×82=410; without the 62 the total is 348, and 348÷4=87.
items.q: A student's five test scores have a mean of 82. If the lowest score, 62, is dropped, what is the mean of the four remaining scores?

items.e: The difference is 5−2=3 parts, so one part is 21÷3=7 students; the class has 2+5=7 parts, or 7×7=49 students.
items.q: In a class, the ratio of students who walk to school to students who ride is 2:5. There are 21 more riders than walkers. How many students are in the class?

items.e: Seven full bags use 7 × 5 = 35 cookies, and 38 − 35 = 3 cookies are left over.
items.q: There are 38 cookies packed into bags of 5. After all the full bags are made, how many cookies are left over?

items.e: Three of the 8 slices are gone, so 8 − 3 = 5 slices remain, which is 5/8 of the pizza.
items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices, and 3 of the slices are eaten. What fraction of the pizza is left?

c: She can buy all three and have $1.00 left
She can buy all three with exactly $0 left
She can buy all three and have $2.00 left
items.q: Dana has $20 and wants to buy items priced $6.85, $4.20, and $7.95. Which statement is true?

items.e: Rounding gives 5,000÷50=100, and the exact quotient is a little under 98, so 100 is the closest estimate.
items.q: Which is the best estimate of 4,982 ÷ 51?

items.e: The four friends total 4×20=80, so all five total 105, and 105÷5=21.
items.q: Four friends have a mean score of 20 in a game. A fifth friend joins with a score of 25. What is the mean score of all five friends?

items.e: Each layer holds 5 × 3 = 15 cubes and the box is 2 layers tall, so 15 × 2 = 30 cubes fill it.
items.q: How many 1-centimeter cubes are needed to fill a box that is 5 cm long, 3 cm wide, and 2 cm tall?

items.e: Since 3 cm stands for 12 m, 1 cm stands for 4 m, so 30 m needs 30÷4=7.5 cm.
items.q: On a scale drawing, 3 cm represents 12 meters. A hallway is actually 30 meters long. How long is that hallway on the drawing?

c: Car A, at 35 miles per gallon
Car B, at 30 miles per gallon
Car B, because it traveled more miles
Neither — both travel 30 miles per gallon
items.e: 150÷5=30 and 210÷7=30, so the two cars have exactly the same rate of 30 miles per gallon.
items.q: Car A travels 150 miles on 5 gallons of gas. Car B travels 210 miles on 7 gallons. Which car goes farther on one gallon?

items.e: Two fifths of the 20 sections is 8 green sections, so the other 20 − 8 = 12 sections are white.
items.q: A spinner has 20 equal sections, and each section is either green or white. The probability of landing on green is 2/5. How many of the sections are white?

items.e: The rectangle's perimeter is 2(12+4)=32 cm, so the square has side 32÷4=8 cm and area 8×8=64 square cm.
items.q: A square and a rectangle have the same perimeter. The rectangle measures 12 cm by 4 cm. What is the area of the square?

items.e: The price rises to $66, and 10% of $66 is $6.60, so the final price is $66−$6.60=$59.40 — less than the original because the second 10% is taken from a larger number.
items.q: The $60 price of a game is raised by 10%, and the new price is later lowered by 10%. What is the final price?

items.e: After the book, 3/5 remains; spending 1/3 of that leaves 2/3 × 3/5 = 2/5 of the start, so 2/5 of the money is $12 and the whole is $30.
items.q: Elena spent 2/5 of her money on a book, then spent 1/3 of what was left on a snack. She has $12 left. How much money did she start with?

items.e: Written as decimals, 3/5=0.6 and 2/3 is about 0.667, so 0.7 is greater than all the others, including 0.68.
items.q: Which of these numbers is the greatest?

items.e: 35/50 = 70/100, so 70% of the students chose soccer.
items.q: In a survey, 35 out of 50 students chose soccer. What percent of the students chose soccer?

items.e: A number divisible by 6 must be even and have a digit sum divisible by 3; 358 is even but 3+5+8=16 is not a multiple of 3, while 132, 246, and 414 pass both tests.
items.q: Which of these numbers is NOT divisible by 6?

items.e: The mode is the value that appears most often, and 3 appears twice while each of the others appears once.
items.q: A list of numbers is 3, 7, 3, 9, and 5. What is the mode of the list?

items.e: In order the values are 4, 6, 9, 11, 15, 20; with six values the median is the mean of the middle two, (9+11)÷2=10.
items.q: What is the median of 4, 9, 11, 15, 6, and 20?

items.e: Counting on by 3s gives 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, so the 6th number in the pattern is 18.
items.q: A number pattern counts by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, ... . What is the 6th number in the pattern?

items.e: Along the edges the cubes fit 4 by 3 by 2, so 4×3×2=24 cubes fill the box.
items.q: How many cubes with edges of 2 cm fit exactly inside a box that is 8 cm by 6 cm by 4 cm?

items.e: 15 = 3 × 5, so 5 divides 15 with nothing left over, while 2, 4, and 6 do not.
items.q: Which of these numbers is a factor of 15?

items.e: Complementary angles total 90°, so x+2x=90 gives x=30° and the larger angle is 2×30=60°.
items.q: Two angles are complementary, and one of them is twice as large as the other. What is the measure of the larger angle?
Which is greater, 3 × 3 × 3 or 5 × 5, and by how much?

items.e: There are 15 buttons in all and 5 of them are black, so the probability is 5/15, which is the same as 1/3.
items.q: A jar holds 15 buttons: 6 are blue, 4 are white, and 5 are black. One button is taken out without looking. What is the probability that it is black?

items.e: If each box holds b books, then 5b+3=43, so 5b=40 and b=8.
items.q: Five boxes each hold the same number of books. When 3 more books are added to the collection, there are 43 books in all. How many books are in each box?

items.e: With width w the length is 3w, so the perimeter is 2(3w+w)=8w=48, giving w=6 cm (and length 18 cm).
items.q: The length of a rectangle is 3 times its width. If the perimeter is 48 cm, what is the width?

items.e: Rounding $2.95 up to $3 gives about 6 notebooks; checking, 6 cost $17.70 and 7 would cost $20.65, which is more than $20.
items.q: Notebooks cost $2.95 each. Maya has $20 and no coupon. What is the greatest number of notebooks she can buy?

items.e: The pool plus walkway measures 14 m by 10 m, or 140 square meters, and the pool covers 60, so the walkway is 140−60=80 square meters.
items.q: A rectangular pool measures 10 m by 6 m. A walkway 2 m wide is built all the way around it. What is the area of the walkway alone?
